name: Records of the Panama Canal (Record Group 185)
repository: United States National Archives, College Park, Maryland
holdings: ~9,240 cartographic items / 125 cubic feet on paper at College Park; Compagnie Universelle general and town-site maps 1881–97; Isthmian Canal Commission lock and dam plans, 1913 route plates; textual labor and administrative series; digitized: construction photographs (series 185-G), land and claims index cards
notes: US official; the dominant archive. PI-91 (1956) inventories the CARTOGRAPHIC series only: ~9,240 items / 125 cu. ft. as of 1955, on paper at College Park - searched 2026-09 via catalog metadata ONLY, never full text. Series: Cie Universelle general maps 1881-1900 (154 items) and detailed maps/plans incl. town-site plans 1881-97 (6,620 items); Cie Nouvelle cross sections/area/sectional maps 1889-99 (~730 items incl. Lago de Bohio and Alhajuela series); Nicaragua CC 1895-99 (447); ICC 1899-1913 (~1,000 incl. lock and dam plans, 1913 route plates); The Panama Canal post-1914 (6 items only - the working cartography stayed in Panama). Appendix II place-name index mined 2026-09 for variants (Bas Matachin, De Lesseps City=Gatun, Alto Emperador, Monkey Hill=Mt Hope, Balboa=La Boca) and settlements (Whitehouse, Vamos Vamos, Pena Blanca, Cartagenita, Palo Grande, Cocoli). Textual records separately inventoried (Giroux, unpublished). Digitized online: 185-G construction photos 1887-1940 (partial), 185-CZ operations c.1938-60, 185-CC color 1979-84, aerial (partial); plus digitized index-card and land/claims series (Indexes to Central Files, Land Transactions, Land Claims/Awards/Deeds, Marriage Licenses). Catalog harvest 2026-09: data/nara/ (10,456 records, 59 names).

name: Museo del Canal Interoceanico holdings
repository: Museo del Canal Interoceanico, Panama City
formats: Books, oral history, cartography, photographs, postcards, memorabilia
holdings: Books; cartography (4% of the reserve); photographs (3%); postcards and memorabilia; Archivo de Historia Oral (onsite only); catalog metadata online, no digital objects served
institution: Museo del Canal Interoceánico de Panamá
notes: Panamanian-side counter-archive. Swept 2026-09-13 via typismuci.museodelcanal.com (Koha OPAC). ASYMMETRY FINDING: unlike LOC/UFDC/IA, the Museo serves NO digital objects remotely — only catalog metadata of physical holdings (the sole images are the site logo + Amazon cover thumbnails). Keyword counts (Zona del Canal 54, mapa 47, fotografía 115) are matches on book description fields, not standalone photo/map records; the reserve's own 4% cartography / 3% photos / 5% postcards are not cataloged online. Town-name recall depends on cataloguers' notes, not full text: Gatun 10, Culebra 7, Chagres 7, Gamboa 7, Paraíso 8, Bohío 4, Emperador 4, Gorgona 1, Matachín 1, Tabernilla 0. Oral History Archive exists but is onsite-only. Concrete yield: 1 record (Chen 2014, biblio 6326) documenting the Chinese-community dimension of Emperador, Gorgona, Matachín, Paraíso incl. a 1908 Chinese-population-by-town census. Also held (physical, undigitized): Tejeira, *Pueblos perdidos* (1962, novel); Araúz Torres, *Los mapas antiguos de Panamá y Darién 1503-1879* (2014). Next step to deepen: email scan request (remote) or on-site visit.

Onsite/reproduction routes documented in REPORT_SILVERMEN.md. | 2026-09-13: the consortium-adjacent WORKER VOICE (IHS 1963 letters) IS digitized on dLOC (S-036) - the institutional registers remain reading-room only; both facts now in evidence.

name: Smithsonian collections
access: Searchable in full text; partly online
holdings: 45,000 'Canal Zone' records, searchable in full text (National Museum of Natural History specimen localities); Fishbaugh photograph album (27 of 100 views digitized); 719 Panama Canal Company photonegatives, captions untranscribed; Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute map library, 1,000+ sheets, onsite only
notes: Three layers (2026-09 survey, data/smithsonian/): (1) Open Access API - 45k 'Canal Zone' records, NMNH specimen localities = independent scientific attestation corpus; drowned hamlets (Barbacoas, Bailamonos, Ahorca Lagarto, Cruz de Juan Gallego) score ZERO - absence extends to natural history. (2) NMAH Archives Center: Fishbaugh album (AC.1021, 27/100 views digitized, read); PCC photonegatives (AC.1116, 719 items, captions NOT transcribed digitally - EAD lists accession numbers only); related albums AC.0708/1015/1039/1040. (3) STRI Library map collection: 1,000+ maps, onsite-only, inventory (Jan 2018) covers cabinets 1-11 only; mostly mid-century AMS topographic sheets incl. 1:25k sheets named Gatun, Frijoles, Las Cruces, Barro Colorado. Sitewide search UIs are bot-walled; API + sirismm EADs are the machine route.

name: Gallica digital library (French canal-era material)
access: Fully digitized (open, remote, searchable in full text)
holdings: Boutan 1880: geological survey naming the whole village chain as canal-line stations; Verbrugghe 1879: narrative of the Wyse-Reclus route reconnaissance; Charles-Roux 1886: official French canal-progress report (Buhio-Soldado "un beau campement"); 23 canal-era maps (cartes), downloadable in full resolution, not yet consulted; searchable in full text remotely
notes: French colonial-canal record; fills the Compagnie Universelle period (1879-1904) that the US archive predates. Swept 2026-09-14 via Gallica SRU + ContentSearch + IIIF (curl-open, User-Agent required). Anchor sources: Boutan 1880 geological survey (names the whole village chain as canal-line stations), Verbrugghe 1879 Wyse-Reclus route narrative, Charles-Roux 1886 progress report (Buhio-Soldado 'un beau campement'; Gorgona/Matachin/Mamei as km-marked route stations). ASYMMETRY: the French colonial-power archive is MORE openly accessible remotely than the Panamanian counter-archive (ARC-04 Museo = onsite/metadata-only). Harvest: data/gallica/. Still open: ANOM (Aix) Compagnie internal records; Gallica canal-era maps (23 cartes found, IIIF-downloadable) not yet pulled.
